model.title: Floodplain Enhancement and Recovery Act
model.meta: Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee · Sen. Patty Murray (D-WA)

summary.text: The bill would ease a federal flood insurance rule that generally bars projects in designated floodways if they would raise the area's base flood elevation. Under the bill, a community could allow an ecosystem restoration project in such a floodway that raises flood elevations, but only if a professional engineer finds the cumulative increase is no more than 1 foot, no insurable structure or critical infrastructure is in the affected area, and the community later submits an analysis of the project's effects to the Federal Emergency Management Agency. Ecosystem restoration projects would be defined as those that change a site's physical, chemical, or biological characteristics to recover or improve the functions of a water resource or floodplain.
